Re-read after 0.54.2. The confirm below still holds: the grounding block does say "provenance" in prose where the payload key is edge["resolution"] (query.py:258) - a synonym, not rot, and both words are the right ones in their place.

Why it went stale: this function gained one line. before_edit now carries knowledge_lag alongside map_lag - the ambient report that N coordinates hold stale knowledge nobody has answered. It rides the same three JSON surfaces map_lag does, by deliberate symmetry: freshness.py established that a map may lag but must never lag SILENTLY, and knowledge had the detection without the telling.

The briefing already showed staleness for THIS coordinate; what was missing was the repo-wide fact, which is what an agent needs to know it broke something elsewhere. Keep both: the per-entity flag answers "is what I am reading trustworthy", the ambient line answers "did I leave a mess".

knowledge_lag counts COORDINATES with unsuperseded stale knowledge, never rows. Counting rows makes a diligent repo shout forever, which is how a warning becomes something people scroll past.

author: agent
text:
Re-read after the payload work. Every long-standing observation below still holds and was checked: "provenance" in prose against edge["resolution"] in the payload is a synonym not rot, the knowledge list is still built through for_display with has_stale counting only unsuperseded entries, the <0.7 threshold and the inheritance walk are unchanged, and map_lag/knowledge_lag still ride together.

WHAT CHANGED, and the reason is that this is an AGENT surface. The briefing listed every caller. On prometheus, before_edit on DirLocker.Lock returned 53,534 characters - roughly 13k tokens for one pre-edit check - of which 36,677 was a 342-entry caller list and 15,947 was radius["direct"] repeating those same 342 qualnames at 100% overlap, measured. For a human, density is clutter you can skip. For an agent it is a budget you cannot.

Three properties now:

  RANKED - production before tests, then the caller's own fan-in, then
  qualname for a stable order. This is not cosmetic: Head.Init has 103
  callers of which 98 are tests, so the five that matter were buried at
  an arbitrary depth.

  BOUNDED - CALLER_CAP = 12. Lock went 53,534 -> 2,173 chars (-96%),
  Head.Init 19,053 -> 2,632 (-87%).

  VISIBLE - direct_callers_total, _shown and _tests ride alongside. A
  list that quietly stops at twelve is a sampled list, and this repo's
  own guard message says nothing is ever sampled silently. The counts
  also carry information the full list did not: "103 callers, 98 tests"
  is a fact about the entity.

radius["direct"] is gone, replaced by direct_count. The names live in
direct_callers; duplicating them was free cost.

TWO FIXTURE ERRORS WORTH NOT REPEATING, both found by falsifying rather
than by the tests passing. First, naming a function test_* inside m.py
proves nothing: is_test_entity classifies by PATH. Second, with files
named m.py and test_m.py the unsorted edge order was ALREADY
production-first, so deleting the sort changed nothing and the ranking
assertion passed on luck. The fixture now uses zz_prod.py and aa_test.py
so the natural order puts tests first and the sort has to do the work.

Also worth knowing: the whole 96% reduction landed with the suite green.
Nothing asserted on the size or completeness of these lists before
test_the_briefing_is_ranked_bounded_and_says_so existed.

The ad-hoc CALLER_CAP and the hand-built total/shown keys are gone, replaced by a call to payload.rank_bound_report.

That matters for the reason the census existed: this function's version was the sixth copy of the rule. Five already existed and two of those reported nothing. A structural pin now forbids a seventh - no module outside payload.py may construct a `<name>_shown` key.

author: agent
text:
Re-read after the Django run. The ranked/bounded/reported properties recorded below are unchanged and still implemented through payload.rank_bound_report; direct_callers_tests still rides as a fact about the entity rather than part of the truncation rule.

TWO THINGS THIS RELEASE FOUND, both on django@cccc004 (59,274 entities, 119,238 edges).

1. THE WARNING NOW CARRIES ITS OWN CONFIDENCE. ListMixin.append has 573 direct callers and ALL 573 are bare-name guesses at 0.60 - ordinary `results.append(x)` across the codebase landing on a GIS mixin. The RESOLVER is right there: it could not type the receiver and refused to claim certainty, which is exactly why they are 0.60 and not 0.95. What was wrong was the sentence built from the number - "WIDELY DEPENDED ON (573 direct callers)" as a headline, with the fact that every one was a guess sitting in a separate grounding block phrased about the whole radius. The claim and the caveat were in different places, so a reader weighs the claim. direct_callers_guessed now rides in the payload and the warning says "ALL of them are low-confidence name guesses ... an upper bound on who depends on you, not a count of who does". LOW_CONFIDENCE is named once and shared with the grounding block; a second 0.7 literal is how two surfaces come to disagree about what a guess is.

2. THE 0.58.0 CENSUS MISSED A LIST, and the reason is worth more than the fix. It measured this function on a Go entity with no inheritance, so inheritance.inherited_unchanged_by never appeared. On django, SimpleTestCase.assertRaisesMessage is inherited unchanged by 2,389 test classes and that ONE field was 133,163 of the briefing's 136,453 characters - 97.6%. 136,453 -> 4,107. A census is only as good as the entity it is run on, and "I measured every tool" is not the same claim as "I measured every field".

FIXTURE NOTE, because it cost three attempts and a skip that hid the failure. Reaching the bare-name tier needs a specific shape: two same-named METHODS is not enough, because resolve() breaks that tie itself (production over test) and reports "exact" at 0.95, so the fallback never runs. What is required is that resolve() go ambiguous AND the fallback's filter leave exactly one candidate - a method plus a module-level FUNCTION of the same name does both, since rule 2 removes the function on an attribute call. The first version of that test skipped on a fixture producing zero callers, which is the failure mode this project names most often: a guard becoming the outcome.

author: agent
text:
Re-read at the review/gate work. Everything recorded below still holds: ranked/bounded/reported callers through payload.rank_bound_report, direct_callers_guessed and the guess-aware warning, and the inheritance lists bounded.

NEW HERE: the knowledge list is bounded too, and this is the third field the 0.58.0 census missed. before_edit on THIS function shipped 12 knowledge entries - 10,587 of a 14,673 character payload - and ELEVEN of the twelve were superseded. Superseded is history, not warning (metadata.for_display draws that line), so history is exactly the right thing to truncate: nothing is lost, it stays on disk, `memway show` reads it.

THE PROPERTY TO PRESERVE: the entry that DECIDES is never cut. The rank is r["superseded"], so the unsuperseded entry sorts first; a bounded list that dropped it would hide the warning and keep the history, which is worse than not bounding at all. Falsified both ways - unbounded, and history-first.

Cap is 6 rather than CAP=12 because these entries are long prose, and rank_bound_report takes the cap as an argument precisely so a surface can choose without a second implementation.

WORTH KNOWING ABOUT THE PIN. The no-reimplementation check flagged review.py for the string 'added_shown' - which was a READ of a report it had been handed, not a construction. The pin claimed "no module may construct a <name>_shown key" and was implemented as "no module may mention that string", so it forbade consuming the very thing it protects. It now inspects dict-literal keys and Store-context subscripts. A check whose implementation is broader than its claim eventually blocks correct code, and the first correct code it blocked was mine.
